nodes.description: Bilateral globus pallidus internus (GPi) deep brain stimulation for medically refractory VPS16-related dystonia. In a multicenter cohort of 26 patients, about three-quarters responded, with greater motor improvement from stimulation of the ventroposterior GPi; spasticity and fixed skeletal deformities present before surgery predicted a poorer response.

evidence.reference_title: Deep Brain Stimulation for VPS16-Related Dystonia: A Multicenter Study.
evidence.snippet: DBS was an effective treatment for three-quarters of patients with pathogenic VPS16 variants in our cohort.

evidence.reference_title: Deep Brain Stimulation for VPS16-Related Dystonia: A Multicenter Study.

nodes.description: VPS16 is a core subunit of the HOPS (homotypic fusion and protein sorting) tethering complex. Heterozygous loss-of-function variants reduce functional VPS16/HOPS, impairing the complex's role in membrane fusion.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-Function Variants in HOPS Complex Genes VPS16 and VPS41 Cause Early Onset Dystonia Associated with Lysosomal Abnormalities.
evidence.snippet: A total of 18 individuals harboring heterozygous loss-of-function VPS16 variants, and one with a microdeletion, were identified.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-Function Variants in HOPS Complex Genes VPS16 and VPS41 Cause Early Onset Dystonia Associated with Lysosomal Abnormalities.
evidence.snippet: VPS16 encodes a subunit of the homotypic fusion and vacuole protein sorting (HOPS) complex, which plays a key role in autophagosome-lysosome fusion.
